title: Sample Preparation Strategies for Mass Spectrometry Imaging of 3D Cell Culture Models
protocol: Culture HCT116 colon carcinoma cell line in a T-25 flask with McCoy's 5A media + 10% fetal bovine serum.
Grow cells until they reach 50-70% confluency in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Release cells using 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution.
Count cells using a hemocytometer and trypan blue staining to check viability and density.
Dilute counted cells with complete medium to achieve a seeding density of 6,000 cells/well or 30,000 cells/ml.
Add 0.19 g of agarose to 10 ml of standard media in a 50 ml conical tube to create a 1.5% agarose solution.
Autoclave the agarose-media mixture for 20 minutes using a water bath.
Aspirate 50 μl of the agarose + media mixture into the 60 central wells of a flat-bottomed 96 well plate.
Add 200 μl of 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the peripheral edge wells instead of the agarose solution.
Allow the agarose mixture in the inner wells to cool to approximately 37 °C before adding cells.
Add 200 μl of the appropriate cell solution containing approximately 6,000 cells to an agarose-coated 96 well plate.
Cover the plate and place it in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 at 37°C for cell growth.
Change cell media every 48 hours or when the media changes color.
Aspirate old media carefully from around the small 3D cell culture at the bottom of the agarose.
Add 200 μl of fresh media gently over the 3D cell culture.
(Optional) Dilute and add chemotherapeutics or other drugs to complete media, then administer 200 μl to each well during media changes.
Monitor 3D cell culture growth by optical microscope until cultures are approximately 1 mm in diameter.
Use a 2 ml serological pipette to gently remove the 3D cell culture from the agarose bed.
Wash the 3D cell cultures with PBS by gently pipetting them into approximately 1 ml PBS in a waiting 24 well plate.
Transfer harvested 3D cell cultures via serological pipet to centrifuge tubes for protein or metabolite extraction.
Embed the 3D cell cultures in gelatin by preparing a solution of ~175 mg/ml gelatin in high purity water.
Mix the gelatin vigorously until it becomes viscous and difficult to manipulate.
Warm the gelatin-containing conical tube in a water bath at ~60 °C until the solution is clear and easy to aspirate.
Take the heated gelatin immediately to the cell culture hood.
Keep the tube with gelatin in a beaker with preheated water at about 60 °C to avoid hardening of the gelatin solution.
Deposit 0.6 ml of warm gelatin solution into the well of a 24 flat-bottomed plate using a 2 ml serological pipette.
Gently deposit the 3D cell cultures immediately on top of the gelatin layer using a different 2 ml pipette to avoid rupturing the 3D structure.
Remove any PBS from the top of the gelatin using a 200 μl pipette if present.
Pipette 0.6 ml of warm gelatin mixture over 3D cell cultures without disturbing their position.
Freeze gelatin-embedded 3D cell cultures at -80°C.
Remove the 24 well plate containing the 3D cell cultures from the freezer.
Warm the bottom of the plate with your hand until a tweezer or scalpel can slide down the side gently.
Smoothly slide the tweezer or scalpel to free the gelatin without thawing the center.
Place a drop of water on the cryostat support and use it to adhere the gelatin disk to the support.
Clean the cryostat blade and glass with 70% ethanol before use.
Use a different part of the blade or a new blade for each 3D cell culture-gelatin disc.
Gently face off excess gelatin until 3D cell cultures become visible.
Slowly slice 3D cell cultures into sections measuring 12-16 μm.
Carefully thaw the slices and mount them on ITO-coated glass slides labeled appropriately.
Store the mounted slices in a desiccator.
Wash slices for intact protein detection in cold 100% acetone, Carnoy's fluid, or 70%/95% isopropanol to remove small molecules such as lipids that could mask signals.
Prepare matrix solution with organic solvent and water containing 0.1% TFA for both small molecule analysis and intact protein detection.
Dissolve sinapic acid in acetonitrile before addition of the TFA:H2O solution for optimal solubility.
Apply appropriate matrix to slices using a suitable method, avoiding matrices known to co-crystalize with gelatin such as ferulic acid.
Apply matrix by handspotting method.
Use a fine-tipped syringe to apply 0.5 μl of the matrix solution on the 3D cell culture slice.
Allow the matrix to crystallize.
Alternatively, use the airbrush method.
Fill a commercial grade airbrush with the matrix solution.
Hold the sprayer 8-12 inches away from the slide and aim a fine spray at the slice.
In between passes, allow the matrix to dry for 1 min to allow for the best crystal formation.
Repeat spraying up to 10-20 times as required to produce an optimal layer of matrix.
Alternatively, use the sublimation method detailed elsewhere.
Dry slides in a desiccator for at least 30 min prior to MALDI-MSI, regardless of the method used.
Fit the slides in an adapter made to hold 75 mm x 25 mm slides.
Load the slide adapter into the instrument.
Select an appropriate calibration standard for the mass range for MALDI-MSI.
For small molecule interrogation, use α-CHCA signals as calibrants.
For protein analysis, spot known protein standards adjacent to the cell cultures.
Calibrate the instrument before method development.
Develop data acquisition methods for the chosen mass range using provided software.
Adjust the mass range for small molecule imaging between 100-1,000 m/z in reflectron mode.
Adjust the mass range for protein imaging between 8,000-25,000 m/z.
Adjust laser power to 60% using calibration solution.
Set frequency to 400 laser shots using calibration solution.
Select ultra small spot size using calibration solution.
Optimize detector gain settings in the main instrument control software.
Tune sample rate parameters in the main instrument control software.
Calibrate electronic gain according to specific instrument requirements.
Save optimized method for use in imaging software.
Suppress ions below the mass range of interest in the instrument control software.
Develop protein data acquisition methods for mid-to-high mass ranges above 3 kDa.
Use linear mode for acquiring data in mid-to-high mass ranges.
Adjust MS instrument parameters using imaging software provided by manufacturer.
Create a new imaging file and folder using established methods.
Select instrument parameters including raster spot size (set to 50 µm).
Set up instrument control method according to previous steps.
Position the area for scanning over the 3D cell culture.
Select three appropriate teach points on the sample sequentially.
Move the laser to each selected teach point in turn.
Obtain an optical photograph from the MALDI-TOF laser control software using 'print screen'.
Start the imaging process through the imaging software, not the instrument control.
Acquire mass spectra from each slice of the 3D cell culture.
Observe masses across the entire sample and those localized to specific areas.
Optionally, perform manual analysis by clicking a mass in the mean spectrum.
Automatically pick masses above a particular threshold using imaging software.
For quality control, examine the distribution of matrix peaks or the mean spectrum.
Perform statistical analyses on extracted datasets with mathematical software like R or Matlab.
Export single spectra in ASCII format for compatibility with various software programs.
Convert individual spectra to mzXML or mzML formats for multi-software readability.
Export data as Analyze (.img) format for MRI and other imaging applications.
Load the dataset into MSiReader using the software's instructions.
Load the dataset into BioMap following its specific guidelines.
Perform post-acquisition processing in the chosen software, including baseline removal.
Normalize the data to ensure consistency across samples.
Conduct principal component analysis on the processed data set.
Execute hierarchical clustering analysis with the prepared data set.
